name: Transseptal robot
full_name: KCL force-sensing robot for transseptal puncture (needle and dilator-sheath manipulator)
group: King's College London (K. Rhode; A. M. Zeidan, Z. Xu, C. E. Mower) with Brunel University London (Y. Noh) and Guy's and St Thomas'
versions: 2023 ICRA (only); 2016: KCL 3-DOF MR-compatible multisegment cardiac catheter steering mechanism (Ataollahi 2016 TBME) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 AT1; Pescio 2025 Table 2 row 10) (belikov2024_evolution; pescio2025_endovascular); 2015-19: KCL (K. Rhode, H. Liu, J. Back) tendon-driven catheter robot with tension sensing (Back 2015; model-free position control Back 2017), likely the same hardware as Z. Zhang 2019 RA-L cable-driven continuum catheter control with Inria (Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 AT2, JEs) (belikov2024_evolution)
target_anatomy: interatrial septum (transseptal puncture before left-atrial ablation)
devices_driven: standard transseptal kit: 8.5 Fr SL0 sheath (St Jude), Torflex dilator (Baylis), BRK-1 Brockenbrough needle (71 cm) (Sec. I)
n_dof_detail: 4 actuated (translation and rotation of needle and of dilator-sheath), 2 task-space DOF
translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (lead screws on NEMA-17 steppers M1, M2 move needle and dilator-sheath carriages)
rotation_detail: NEMA-17 steppers M3, M4 rotate needle and sheath continuously
force_sensing: optoelectronic sensors (New Japan Radio) in the tool fixtures measure contact and puncture force along one axis
validation_detail: puncture experiments on anthropomorphic fossa-ovalis tissue models (Sec. IV)
key_numbers: puncture force 3.97 +- 0.45 N (1 SD), similar to manual values in the literature (abstract)
